artifact_role: exact content-bound prabirshrestha/vim-lsp subject authority for downstream Vim proof, receipts, and documentation consumers (#11369)
claim_boundary: configuration_documented substrate only. This object records which exact upstream bytes are targeted and what upstream metadata says. It claims no host behavior, no support tier, no public artifact, and no current upstream state beyond the recorded observation instant.

upstream.commit_subject: Fix respond to client/registerCapability and client/unregisterCapability (#1685)
upstream.selected_ref_note: The pin is the commit and its tree bytes, never a floating branch name.

latest_release_tag_observation.relation_to_pin: the pin is not a released tag object: it is the 2026-08-10 master head, while the newest observed release tag points at a 2021-01-13 commit; no released version string corresponds to the pinned bytes

plugin_load_mode.description: The consumer supplies VIM_LSP_DIR pointing at a clean git checkout of exactly selected_commit; the plugin directory is prepended to 'runtimepath' and plugin/lsp.vim is sourced explicitly after global flags are set.

expected_content_identity.runtimepath_entry_identity: the exact VIM_LSP_DIR checkout whose HEAD resolves to upstream.selected_commit with a clean worktree

entry_files.role: global flag defaults and plugin entry

expected_content_identity.resolution_rule: a checkout satisfies this subject only when every listed entry file's git blob SHA1 and the checkout HEAD's commit match this manifest

upstream_theoretical_prerequisites.maintained_floor_authority: #10966 owns any future maintained/tested Vim version row; nothing here may be projected into support state

optional_acceleration.detail: g:lsp_use_lua defaults to has('nvim-0.4.0') || (has('lua') && has('patch-8.2.0775')); absence degrades performance, not correctness

snippets.model: not supported by default; snippet insertion requires a third-party snippet plugin plus a vim-lsp integration plugin
snippets.consequence_for_drivers: canonical drivers must treat plain-text completion items as the ordinary wire shape and must not require snippetSupport

sources.note: vim-lsp does not support snippets by default

completion_channel.model: omnifunc lsp#complete; asynchronous completion optional via g:lsp_async_completion

semantic_highlighting.model: unofficial vscode semantic-token extension, requires Neovim highlights or Vim textprop; not exercised by the canonical driver

pin_governance.replacement_law: A newer upstream master head or a matching display version does not replace this pin; replacement requires a reviewed manifest update that re-resolves commit and tree bytes.
pin_governance.floating_branch_policy: floating branch/master references are invalid anywhere a subject identity is consumed

current_upstream_comparison.interpretation: at the observation instant the pin coincided with upstream master; that coincidence carries no forward durability

pin_governance.future_refresh_rule: a separate read-only upstream refresh comparison may detect drift; it cannot mutate this pin or any support state automatically

last_deliberate_verification.method: git ls-remote ref observation plus depth-1 fetch of selected_commit resolving commit and tree digests locally
last_deliberate_verification.verification_boundary: this verifies byte identity of the pinned subject only; it observed no editor behavior
